questions.stem: Which among the following is a protein-coding RNA?
questions.solutionHtml:
mRNA is a protein-coding RNA.

The mRNA convey genetic information from DNA to the ribosome, where they specify the amino acid sequence of the protein products of gene expression.





Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page no: 355

questions.stem: Which of the following RNA is not directly involved in protein synthesis?
questions.solutionHtml:
miRNA is not directly involved in protein synthesis. miRNA participates in the modulation of gene expression by altering mRNA function.

The mRNAs, rRNAs, and tRNAs are directly involved in protein synthesis. Other RNAs participate in either mRNA splicing (snRNAs) or modulation of gene expression by altering mRNA function (mi/siRNAs) and/or expression (lncRNAs).





Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page nos: 355

questions.stem: Which of the following is true?

options.label: A
options.text: Primer is involved in RNA synthesis

options.label: B
options.text: Highly active efficient proofreading function in RNA transcription

options.label: C
options.text: Deoxyribonucleotides are used in RNA synthesis

options.label: D
options.text: U replaces T as the complementary base for A in RNA

questions.answerText: U replaces T as the complementary base for A in RNA
questions.solutionHtml:
Uracil (U) replaces thymine (T)  as the complementary base for adenine (A) in RNA.






Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page no: 355

questions.stem: Which enzyme is responsible for the polymerization of ribonucleotides into a sequence complementary to the template strand of the gene?
questions.solutionHtml:
DNA-dependent RNA polymerase is the enzyme responsible for the polymerization of ribonucleotides into a sequence complementary to the template strand of the gene.

The enzyme attaches at a specific site, the promoter, on the template strand. This is followed by the initiation of RNA synthesis at the starting point, and the process continues until a termination sequence is reached.





Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page no 354, 386

questions.stem: Which enzyme prevents the formation of superhelical tensions in the DNA during transcription?
questions.solutionHtml:
Topoisomerase prevents the formation of superhelical tensions in the DNA during transcription.

During transcription, supercoils form when the DNA is unwound and can add stress to the molecule. Topoisomerase activity enables RNA elongation to proceed further without being stopped. This action of topoisomerase also takes place during DNA replication.





Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page no 351

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a function of RNA polymerase II?
questions.solutionHtml:
Synthesis of rRNA is not a function of RNA polymerase II. This is done by RNA polymerase I





Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page no 355

questions.stem: The role of the sigma factor in bacterial RNA polymerase is to ____________.

options.label: B
options.text: Position RNA polymerase correctly on the template DNA

questions.answerText: Position RNA polymerase correctly on the template DNA
questions.solutionHtml:
The σ subunit (sigma factor) enables RNA polymerase to recognize promoter regions on the DNA and thus helps to position it correctly on the template DNA.





Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page: 354

questions.stem: During a field trip, an 11-year-old boy consumes a wild mushroom which was later identified to be a death cap mushroom. Which of the following enzymes is inhibited by the toxin from this mushroom?
questions.solutionHtml:
The mushroom death cap (also known as Amanita phalloides) produces the toxin, α-amanitin which inhibits RNA polymerase.

In eukaryotes, α-Amanitin forms a tight complex with the polymerase, thereby inhibiting mRNA synthesis and, ultimately, protein synthesis.

Note: Rifampicin inhibits the prokaryotic DNA-dependent RNA polymerase.





Lippincott's Illustrated Reviews Series Biochemistry 5th edition Paperback – 2010, Page no: 424
Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page no: 388

questions.stem: Which enzyme gives signals for termination of RNA transcription?
questions.solutionHtml:
RNA polymerase II gives signals for the termination of RNA transcription. Proteins catalyzing RNA processing, termination, and polyadenylation appear to load onto RNA polymerase II soon after initiation.

Termination of transcription can be:

  • ρ dependent: When the termination signals are met, ρ factor binds to RNA. ρ factor has ATP dependent helicase activity. It detaches the RNA from the DNA.
  • ρ independent: In the 3' end of RNA, there is a series of U. RNA detaches from DNA due to weaker A=U at the end.




Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page no 392-393

questions.stem: RNA produced from a fragment of DNA has the sequence of UAAGGC. The sequence of the non-template strand in the DNA that gave rise to this sequence is which one of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
The non-template strand or coding strand in the DNA will have the same sequence of the RNA that is produced, except that the non-template or coding strand has T is in place of U. 

As all sequences are written in the 5′ to 3′ direction, unless otherwise specified, an RNA sequence of UAAGGC would correspond to a DNA sequence, on the non-template strand, of TAAGGC. Both the non-template strand and RNA produced will be a complementary sequence to the template strand. Therefore, the template strand would be ATTCCG (written 5′ to 3′).






Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page no 376

questions.stem: What is a primary transcript?

options.label: A
options.text: RNA product synthesized in the 5′-3′ direction

options.label: B
options.text: RNA product synthesized in the 3′-5′ direction

options.label: C
options.text: DNA product synthesized in the 3′-5′ direction

options.label: D
options.text: DNA product synthesized in the 5′-3′ direction

questions.answerText: RNA product synthesized in the 5′-3′ direction
questions.solutionHtml:
The RNA product, which is synthesized in the 5′-3′ direction, is the primary transcript. The primary transcripts are generated by RNA polymerase II.

The longest primary transcript is produced by the dystrophin gene.






Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page no: 387

questions.stem: 7-methyl-guanosine triphosphate capping of the primary transcript is necessary for _____.

options.label: A
options.text: Processing of the primary transcript to mRNA

options.label: C
options.text: Protection of the mRNA against nucleolytic attack by 5′-exonucleases

questions.solutionHtml:
7-methyl-guanosine triphosphate capping of primary transcript is necessary for:

  • Processing of the primary transcript to mRNA
  • Translation of the mRNA
  • Protection of the mRNA against nucleolytic attack by 5′-exonucleases




Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page no 355

questions.stem: The attachment of Eukaryotic mRNA to the ribosome is mediated through ________
questions.solutionHtml:
The attachment of mRNA to the ribosome is mediated through the guanyl cap at the 5' end. Eukaryotic mRNAs have 7-methylguanosine caps at the 5' end and poly-A tails at the 3' end.

The 7-methylguanosine caps (Guanyl caps) are necessary for:

  • Processing of primary transcripts to mRNA.
  • Mediating the attachment of mRNA to the ribosome for translation.
  • Protection of mRNA against nucleolytic attack by 5'exonucleases.

Other options:

Option A: AAUAAA is present at the 3’ end, which is the polyadenylation sequence (poly-A tail). They help stabilize the mRNA, facilitate its exit from the nucleus and aid in translation. After the mRNA enters the cytosol, the poly-A tail is gradually shortened.

Option B: tRNA molecules serve as adapters for the translation of the information in the sequence of nucleotides of the mRNA into specific amino acids.

Option D: Shine-Dalgarno sequence initiates translation in prokaryotes.

Note: The guanyl cap and poly-A tail aid in attaching the mRNA to the ribosome for translation, however, it is initiated and mediated first through the Guanyl cap.  The poly(A) tail stimulates recruitment of the 40S ribosomal subunit to the mRNA, after which the ribosomal subunit binds to the guanyl cap at 5'end of mRNA. 





Online Resource, Cooper GM. The Cell: A Molecular Approach. 2nd edition. Sunderland (MA): Sinauer Associates; 2000. Translation of mRNA. Available from: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK9849/
Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page no 355, 400

questions.stem: After synthesis, eukaryotic mRNA undergoes extensive modifications including which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
After synthesis, eukaryotic RNA undergoes extensive post-transcriptional modifications including 7-methylguanosine capping, polyadenylation forming poly A tail and splicing

  • 5' Capping: This is the first of the processing reactions for pre mRNA. The cap is a 7-methylguanosine attached backward to the 5'-terminal end of the mRNA, forming an unusual 5'→5' triphosphate linkage.
  • Poly-A tail is added after transcription by the nuclear enzyme, polyadenylate polymerase, using ATP as the substrate. These tails help stabilize the mRNA, facilitate its exit from the nucleus, and aid in translation.
  • Maturation of eukaryotic mRNA usually involves the removal of introns & joining of exons together to form the mature mRNA. The process of removing introns and joining exons is called splicing. snRNA facilitates the removal of introns by forming base pairs with the consensus sequences at each end of the intron.





Lippincott's Illustrated Reviews Series Biochemistry 5th edition Paperback – 2010, Page 426
Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, page 397-398

questions.stem: Which of the following does not require 5’ capping?
questions.solutionHtml:
tRNA of Alanine does not require 5’ capping.

Capping process protects the 5′ end of mRNA from the action of exonucleases and polyadenylation protects the 3′ end of the mRNA. All mRNA, snRNA, and siRNA undergo this process, but tRNA are comparatively stable and do not require a capping at the 5’ end.

Note: rRNAs also do not require 5' capping.





Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page no 354-355
Online Resource, Hou YM, Gamper H, Yang W. Post-transcriptional modifications to tRNA--a response to the genetic code degeneracy. RNA. 2015;21(4):642-644. doi:10.1261/rna.049825.115

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about mRNA splicing is true?

options.label: A
options.text: The existence of split genes has no advantage

options.label: B
options.text: Self-splicing introns do not require the help of any protein for splicing to occur accurately

options.label: C
options.text: β-thalassaemia results from a genetic defect in the spliceosome

questions.answerText: Self-splicing introns do not require the help of any protein for splicing to occur accurately
questions.solutionHtml:
Self-splicing introns do not require a spliceosome or any other proteins for the splicing reaction.

Self-splicing introns fold into complex loops and undergo transesterification reactions, thus undergoing self splicing. 

Other options:

Option A: Split genes have the advantage that they allow alternative splicing so that a single gene can code for variant forms of the same protein.

Option C: β-thalassemia results from the faulty splicing of the β-globin transcript. However, the spliceosome is normal and the reason for the fault is a mutation in the β-globin gene itself.

Option D: Splicing occurs in the nucleus and mature transcripts are then transported into the cytosol for translation (protein synthesis) to occur.






Lippincott's Illustrated Reviews Series Biochemistry 5th edition Paperback – 2010, Pg 426, 427
Online Resource, https://www.nature.com/scitable/topicpage/rna-splicing-introns-exons-and-spliceosome-12375/

questions.stem: Which of the following does not happen in 5' to 3' direction?
questions.solutionHtml:
RNA editing occurs in 3’ to 5’ direction. It is the process by which the coding sequence is changed at the mRNA level before translation.
RNA editing occurs by insertion of additional Us at the 3’ end of the mRNA and proceeds in a 3’ to 5’ direction. The guide RNA (gRNA) acts as a template for the editing process. An example of RNA editing is apoB gene and mRNA shown in the image below:

questions.stem: The eukaryotic initiation factor (eIF) that helps in cap binding is?
questions.solutionHtml:
The eukaryotic initiation factor (eIF) that helps in cap binding is eIF 4.

eIF are accessory proteins that help initiate protein synthesis.

Functions of eIF:

  • eIF3 & eIF 1A: First step of initiation involves dissociation of the ribosome into its 40S and 60S subunits. eIF3 & eIF 1A bind to newly dissociated 40s ribosomal subunit and hence delays the association of 40s and 60s.
  • eIF2: It is involved in the formation of binary complex (GTP+eIF). This complex binds to met t RNA. Further, the GTP-eIF-2-tRNAi ternary complex binds to the 40S ribosomal subunit to form the 43S preinitiation complex. This is the second step of initiation.
  • eIF4: It forms the cap binding complex.  It binds to 5′ terminal of mRNA molecules which are capped. The mRNA would then bind to the 43S preinitiation complex to form the 48S initiation complex, in the third step of initiation.
  • eIF5: It is involved in the hydrolysis of GTP bound to eIF2. This results in binding of 60s subunit with 48s initiation complex to form the 80s initiation complex. This is the fourth step of initiation.





Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page no: 411-412

questions.stem: Which statement best explains the function of eEF-2?

options.label: A
options.text: It is required for the translocation of peptidyl-tRNA during translation

options.label: B
options.text: It is required for the initiation of protein synthesis

options.label: C
options.text: It is the agent that binds to, and is inactivated by, chloramphenicol

options.label: D
options.text: It functions as a peptidyl transferase

questions.answerText: It is required for the translocation of peptidyl-tRNA during translation
questions.solutionHtml:
Eukaryotic elongation factor 2 (eEF-2) is required for the translocation of peptidyl-tRNA along the mRNA during translation.

The elongation reaction requires GTP hydrolysis. The corresponding elongation factor in bacteria is EF-G. Diphtheria toxin ADP-ribosylates eEF-2, leading to its inactivation.

Other options:

Option B: Initiation of eukaryotic protein synthesis requires several initiation factors, designated eIF-1, eIF-2, etc.

Option C: Chloramphenicol inhibits prokaryotic peptidyl transferase.

Option D: Peptidyl transferase is an rRNA (within the large ribosomal subunit) involved in formation of the peptide bond between the amino acid groups within the A and P sites of the ribosome.





Lippincott's Illustrated biochemisty 6th Edition, Page nos 440-441
Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page no: 413

questions.stem: The process of apolipoprotein B48 synthesis involves which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
The process of apolipoprotein B48 synthesis involves RNA editing.
 
RNA editing is the process by which the coding sequence of the mRNA is changed before translation. As a result, the mRNA template differs from the DNA from which it was transcribed. This leads to the formation of a different protein. This occurs by insertion of additional uracils at the 3’ end of the mRNA and proceeds in 3’ to 5’ direction.
 
RNA editing in apoB synthesis:
  • In the liver, the apoB gene is transcribed to mRNA which is then translated to apoB 100.
  • In the intestine, the same apoB gene is transcribed to the same mRNA. But now, the mRNA undergoes editing by an enzyme cytidine deaminase which converts the CAA codon in the mRNA to UAA at a single specific site. This edited mRNA translates to apoB 48.





Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page no: 402
Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, 8th edition, Page no: 1111-1113

questions.stemHtml: The illustration below shows alternative splicing of a gene which has intron segments 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5. It yields two products A and B, by the action of different promoters. You are provided with the promoters w, x, y, and z, each of which binds to a different segment as shown below and acts in the marked direction. Which of the following promoters will you use to get product A?
questions.solutionHtml:
Among the given options, using primers W and Y will yield the desired product A.

Promoters or DNA regulatory elements usually precedes the desired exon to be transcribed. It helps redirect transcription of only the desired exons of a gene to yield a product. Alternative splicing utilizes different promoters to code slightly different products from the same gene. 

In this question, the desired product A has segments 1,3,4,5 whilst the other product B has 1,2,4,5. The difference between both is the presence of seg 3 in product A and the presence of seg 2 in product B. As the product in question is A, only seg 3 is required while excluding seg 2 and ensuring seg 1,4 and 5 intact.

  • Seg 1- Needs to be transcribed and so W is essential
  • Seg 2- Does not need to be transcribed.
  • Seg 3- Needs to be transcribed and so Y is essential
  • Seg 4- Needs to be transcribed but Z is not essential as Y continues the transcription in the direction shown by the arrow. 

The answer is hence promoter W and Y.





Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Pg 399-401
